narrations.en: The last 14 steps, the proof is finally complete! Starting from the definition (assumption) of an isosceles triangle that the lengths of the two sides AB and AC are the same in triangle ABC, which was the starting assumption, and going through the critical auxiliary line of drawing the green angle bisector AD, which divides the vertex angle A exactly in half, to the base BC, we confirmed without a single flaw that the conclusion was held that the two base angles B and C opposite the two sides of the same length are the same size (angle B = angle C). As a math teacher, what I really want to ask is that in order to avoid using the conclusion to be proved (two base angles are equal) in advance during the proof process, you must draw an auxiliary line bisector of the vertex angles and derive it as SAS congruence to avoid falling into circular logic. Lastly, ask yourself a deeper question. If, instead of the bisector of the vertex angle, we draw an auxiliary line (median line) connecting the midpoint M of the base BC, under what congruence condition (SSS congruence) can we prove the same? Experiment by moving the shapes directly on the math homepage in the link in the description!
